correctness.rationale: The all-three-success event is exactly the conjunction of exterior A clocks following their earliest adjacent B clock. The necessity follows because an earlier A adsorbs and blocks a future B; sufficiency follows by induction in B arrival order. Integrating independent unit-rate exponential clocks over the 6 B arrival permutations gives 1/48 for 8-boundary straight trimers and 2/63 for 7-boundary bent trimers. A separate integer permutation-subset dynamic program confirms both fractions, the published two-seed 1/16 benchmark, and the counting of connected triples; 171 exact assertions passed. The 64/85 fraction follows from 2L^2 straight and 4L^2 bent configurations for each L>=7. The proof covers all finite L>=7 and does not use numerical extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Martins, Dickman and Ziff (arXiv:2211.04622, Sec. III.2) explicitly analyze two designated B arrivals and report pair probabilities, including the 1/16 adjacent-pair outcome. Their suggestion that higher-order methods are possible does not report the distinct straight- and bent-three-seed success probabilities or their conditional shape-selection ratio. Comparing the actual statements, a pair-acceptance probability cannot fix the three-body neighborhood-overlap counts. Targeted searches did not locate an explicit prior formula for 1/48, 2/63 and 64/85 in this model; priority remains conditional on further independent scholarship.
residual_risks: General linear-extension or competition-graph identities may implicitly specialize to the exact fractions; independent bibliographic comparison is not performed.

value.rationale: The first connected minority cluster size with a nontrivial shape classification on a square lattice is three, comprising line and corner trimers. Their exact acceptance probabilities differ by a factor 32/21 and the bent fraction among successful connected seeds is 64/85 rather than the pure combinatorial 2/3; this directly quantifies geometrically induced local aggregation in a physically motivated antagonistic-deposition probe studied at the one- and two-seed levels in the motivating literature. The complete shape distribution and size-independent exactness make this a natural, motivated finite invariant, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The result is deliberately not overextended to full mixed-color jamming coefficients.
